status: Design roadmap; shared implementation documented in docs/studio-ux-implementation.md
method: Inventory from the local 16-studio, 96-lab registry. Thirty shared review dimensions are tailored to each lab’s controls, evidence, visual explanation and existing theory. Priorities are proposed sequencing, not measured severity. Suggestions may refine existing features; this is not a new defect audit.

suggestions.title: First-minute goal
suggestions.proposal: Open with one concrete task involving left and right endpoint positions; show the expected observation involving endpoint difference with reading uncertainty before introducing advanced controls.

suggestions.title: Control hierarchy
suggestions.proposal: Group left and right endpoint positions in a primary control section; move display-only preferences to a separate section so changing the model and changing its view are distinguishable.

suggestions.title: Precise adjustment
suggestions.proposal: Pair adjustments for left and right endpoint positions with editable values, unit labels and small-step buttons; retain an equivalent non-drag interaction wherever a handle is used.

suggestions.title: Evidence hierarchy
suggestions.proposal: Give endpoint difference with reading uncertainty a persistent result area with stable number widths, clear units and precision appropriate to the model.

suggestions.title: Direct visual linkage
suggestions.proposal: Connect control focus to a highlight in eye position and parallax sight line; remove the highlight on blur so the visualization does not accumulate distracting emphasis.

suggestions.title: Predict before reveal
suggestions.proposal: In Predict, ask what happens to endpoint difference with reading uncertainty when one element of left and right endpoint positions changes; save the prediction and reveal the comparison only after the learner runs the case.

suggestions.title: Experiment checklist
suggestions.proposal: Turn this investigation into selectable steps with a recording slot per step: Hold length fixed, vary eye angle, then compare reading one endpoint obliquely with reading both at the same angle.

suggestions.title: Explain at the observation
suggestions.proposal: In Explain, place an expandable annotation beside eye position and parallax sight line that connects the visible behavior to: A length is a difference between coordinates, not an endpoint reading. Reading both ends also permits use of a rule whose zero is worn. The eye must lie on the normal through the graduation being read.

suggestions.title: Challenge progression
suggestions.proposal: Offer a guided challenge about endpoint difference with reading uncertainty, then the same task with hints hidden; score the reasoning and final state separately.

suggestions.title: Tab continuity
suggestions.proposal: Preserve left and right endpoint positions, recorded evidence and scroll position when switching Observe, Predict, Experiment, Explain and Challenge; expose the active mode in a shareable URL.

suggestions.title: Tab interaction refinement
suggestions.proposal: For this lab’s mode strip, verify arrow-key navigation, visible focus, selected state and panel association; returning from theory should restore focus to the originating Meter Scale control.

suggestions.title: Equation-to-scene mapping
suggestions.proposal: Allow each term in “L = xR − xL; apparent shift = h tan θ” to highlight its corresponding readout or element of eye position and parallax sight line; provide a plain-text explanation alongside symbols.

suggestions.title: Units drawer
suggestions.proposal: Add a compact units and symbols drawer next to the equation: xR, xL and height h in cm; θ from the surface normal; L in cm. Keep units visible even when that drawer is closed.

suggestions.title: Worked-example replay
suggestions.proposal: Make the existing worked example replayable as ordered steps, highlighting the substituted quantities before showing the result: An object extends from 12.3 to 16.6 cm. L = 16.6 − 12.3. L = 4.3 cm; a shared +0.2 cm endpoint offset cancels before rounding.

suggestions.title: Derivation stepper
suggestions.proposal: Present the derivation one step at a time with Back and Show all controls. The first annotated step should be: Choose an origin on the graduation plane.

suggestions.title: Misconception feedback
suggestions.proposal: When a prediction conflicts with the model, offer a targeted comparison around this misconception rather than a generic wrong-answer message: A 1 mm division is resolution, not a guarantee of 1 mm accuracy. Calibration and parallax are separate effects.

suggestions.title: Assumptions in context
suggestions.proposal: Place a concise model-limit badge beside endpoint difference with reading uncertainty; expand it to show: The lab rounds each endpoint to the selected division. Equal raised heights and identical sight-line angles are needed for parallax cancellation. Separate rounding can prevent exact cancellation.

suggestions.title: Paired comparison
suggestions.proposal: Let learners pin a baseline and compare a second setting of left and right endpoint positions; align the two views of eye position and parallax sight line and show changes in endpoint difference with reading uncertainty.

suggestions.title: Trial notebook
suggestions.proposal: Add a trial table that records left and right endpoint positions, endpoint difference with reading uncertainty and a learner note; include undo for removing a row and a clear indication of which trial is currently displayed.

suggestions.title: Inspectable evidence
suggestions.proposal: Provide an inspect mode for endpoint difference with reading uncertainty: synchronized cursor values for continuous plots, or selectable labeled rows for discrete states; keep the inspected point visible in eye position and parallax sight line.

suggestions.title: Reversible exploration
suggestions.proposal: Provide named baseline reset and one-step undo for changes to left and right endpoint positions; preview what a reset will replace when recorded trials are present.

suggestions.title: Narrow-screen layout
suggestions.proposal: On a narrow screen, keep eye position and parallax sight line above the primary left and right endpoint positions controls, and make endpoint difference with reading uncertainty available through a compact sticky summary without covering tab content.

suggestions.title: Redundant visual encoding
suggestions.proposal: Use labels plus line styles, shapes or arrowheads in eye position and parallax sight line; make the comparison understandable in grayscale and avoid relying on color alone.

suggestions.title: Accessible evidence summary
suggestions.proposal: Expose a readable summary of endpoint difference with reading uncertainty and the selected state of eye position and parallax sight line; announce user-triggered changes at a controlled rate rather than announcing every animation frame.

suggestions.title: Visual density control
suggestions.proposal: Offer essential and detailed annotation levels for eye position and parallax sight line; retain units and the main endpoint difference with reading uncertainty readout in both modes.

suggestions.title: Motion and rendering preference
suggestions.proposal: If eye position and parallax sight line animates, offer pause, slower playback and reduced-motion presentation; for a static view, offer a simplified rendering option that retains all numerical evidence.

suggestions.title: Reasoning self-check
suggestions.proposal: Present this self-check with an optional hint and a separate answer reveal: Two independent endpoints each have standard uncertainty 0.03 cm. What is u(L)? Preserve the learner’s reasoning when revealing the explanation.

suggestions.title: Extension pathway
suggestions.proposal: Add an optional “Beyond this model” activity after the core task: For correlated readings, u²(L) = u²(xR) + u²(xL) − 2 cov(xR,xL). Common zero error cancels, while independent reading noise does not. State when it is a conceptual extension rather than something the current simulator calculates.

suggestions.title: Reproducible sharing
suggestions.proposal: Create a share/export summary containing left and right endpoint positions, endpoint difference with reading uncertainty, model assumptions and lab version; offer a text alternative to the visual snapshot of eye position and parallax sight line.

suggestions.title: Studio learning connection
suggestions.proposal: End the session with a concise evidence-based recap of endpoint difference with reading uncertainty, the saved prediction and one next-lab link within Measurement Studio; explain the conceptual connection before navigation.

suggestions.title: Experiment checklist
suggestions.proposal: Turn this investigation into selectable steps with a recording slot per step: Remove the wire, close the spindle and inspect zero. Reinsert it and compare corrected readings for both correction signs.

suggestions.title: Explain at the observation
suggestions.proposal: In Explain, place an expandable annotation beside unwrapped sleeve and thimble scales that connects the visible behavior to: A precision screw converts rotation into axial displacement. The sleeve counts half-millimetre pitches; the thimble resolves each pitch into 50 divisions. The ratchet in a physical instrument limits contact force.

suggestions.proposal: Offer a guided challenge about pitch and least-count calculation, then the same task with hints hidden; score the reasoning and final state separately.

suggestions.title: Equation-to-scene mapping
suggestions.proposal: Allow each term in “LC = pitch/N = 0.5/50 = 0.01 mm; d = sleeve + thimble + correction” to highlight its corresponding readout or element of unwrapped sleeve and thimble scales; provide a plain-text explanation alongside symbols.

suggestions.title: Units drawer
suggestions.proposal: Add a compact units and symbols drawer next to the equation: Pitch in mm/revolution; N = 50; correction is negative zero error. Keep units visible even when that drawer is closed.

suggestions.title: Worked-example replay
suggestions.proposal: Make the existing worked example replayable as ordered steps, highlighting the substituted quantities before showing the result: Sleeve = 0.5 mm and thimble = 3 divisions; correction = −0.03 mm. Raw = 0.5 + 0.03 = 0.53 mm. Wire diameter = 0.50 mm.

suggestions.title: Derivation stepper
suggestions.proposal: Present the derivation one step at a time with Back and Show all controls. The first annotated step should be: Count complete half-millimetres exposed on the sleeve.

suggestions.title: Misconception feedback
suggestions.proposal: When a prediction conflicts with the model, offer a targeted comparison around this misconception rather than a generic wrong-answer message: Zero correction and zero error have opposite signs. A displayed correction is added, whereas a measured zero error is subtracted.

suggestions.title: Assumptions in context
suggestions.proposal: Place a concise model-limit badge beside pitch and least-count calculation; expand it to show: The simulation represents rigid contact and a calibrated pitch. Backlash, screw eccentricity and contact compression require separate evaluation in real measurements.

suggestions.title: Paired comparison
suggestions.proposal: Let learners pin a baseline and compare a second setting of thimble rotation and zero correction; align the two views of unwrapped sleeve and thimble scales and show changes in pitch and least-count calculation.

suggestions.title: Reversible exploration

suggestions.proposal: On a narrow screen, keep unwrapped sleeve and thimble scales above the primary thimble rotation and zero correction controls, and make pitch and least-count calculation available through a compact sticky summary without covering tab content.

suggestions.title: Redundant visual encoding
suggestions.proposal: Use labels plus line styles, shapes or arrowheads in unwrapped sleeve and thimble scales; make the comparison understandable in grayscale and avoid relying on color alone.

suggestions.title: Accessible evidence summary
suggestions.proposal: Expose a readable summary of pitch and least-count calculation and the selected state of unwrapped sleeve and thimble scales; announce user-triggered changes at a controlled rate rather than announcing every animation frame.

suggestions.title: Visual density control
suggestions.proposal: Offer essential and detailed annotation levels for unwrapped sleeve and thimble scales; retain units and the main pitch and least-count calculation readout in both modes.

suggestions.title: Motion and rendering preference
suggestions.proposal: If unwrapped sleeve and thimble scales animates, offer pause, slower playback and reduced-motion presentation; for a static view, offer a simplified rendering option that retains all numerical evidence.

suggestions.title: Reasoning self-check
suggestions.proposal: Present this self-check with an optional hint and a separate answer reveal: A screw advances 1 mm in two turns. With 100 divisions per turn, what is least count? Preserve the learner’s reasoning when revealing the explanation.

suggestions.title: Extension pathway
suggestions.proposal: Add an optional “Beyond this model” activity after the core task: For a wire area A = πd²/4, first-order relative uncertainty is u(A)/A ≈ 2u(d)/d, so small diameter errors strongly affect inferred area. State when it is a conceptual extension rather than something the current simulator calculates.

suggestions.title: Experiment checklist
suggestions.proposal: Turn this investigation into selectable steps with a recording slot per step: Reduce sag toward zero and compare radius uncertainty with curvature uncertainty. Reverse convex/concave and inspect the sign.

suggestions.title: Explain at the observation
suggestions.proposal: In Explain, place an expandable annotation beside sphere cross-section and sagitta that connects the visible behavior to: Three feet define a reference plane. The central screw measures sagitta h relative to that plane. The support-circle radius r is not the separation between adjacent feet; the latter is √3 r.

suggestions.title: Challenge progression
suggestions.proposal: Offer a guided challenge about curvature radius with propagated uncertainty, then the same task with hints hidden; score the reasoning and final state separately.

suggestions.title: Equation-to-scene mapping
suggestions.proposal: Allow each term in “R = (r² + h²)/(2h); curvature κ = ±1/R” to highlight its corresponding readout or element of sphere cross-section and sagitta; provide a plain-text explanation alongside symbols.

suggestions.title: Units drawer
suggestions.proposal: Add a compact units and symbols drawer next to the equation: r, h and R in mm; κ in mm⁻¹; plus for the chosen convex convention. Keep units visible even when that drawer is closed.

suggestions.title: Worked-example replay
suggestions.proposal: Make the existing worked example replayable as ordered steps, highlighting the substituted quantities before showing the result: r = 30 mm and h = 0.42 mm. R = (900 + 0.1764)/0.84. R ≈ 1071.64 mm; convex κ ≈ 9.332×10⁻⁴ mm⁻¹.

suggestions.title: Derivation stepper
suggestions.proposal: Present the derivation one step at a time with Back and Show all controls. The first annotated step should be: Draw the sphere centre, a foot and the central surface point.

suggestions.title: Misconception feedback
suggestions.proposal: When a prediction conflicts with the model, offer a targeted comparison around this misconception rather than a generic wrong-answer message: Do not substitute foot-to-foot separation into the support-radius formula. If separation is l, use R = l²/(6h) + h/2.

suggestions.title: Assumptions in context
suggestions.proposal: Place a concise model-limit badge beside curvature radius with propagated uncertainty; expand it to show: All three feet lie on a spherical surface with equal support radius. At h = 0 the surface is flat: R diverges while curvature is zero. Small-sag radius uncertainty can become very large.

suggestions.proposal: Provide named baseline reset and one-step undo for changes to leg spacing and central screw height; preview what a reset will replace when recorded trials are present.

suggestions.title: Motion and rendering preference
suggestions.proposal: If sphere cross-section and sagitta animates, offer pause, slower playback and reduced-motion presentation; for a static view, offer a simplified rendering option that retains all numerical evidence.

suggestions.title: Reasoning self-check
suggestions.proposal: Present this self-check with an optional hint and a separate answer reveal: For l = 30 mm and h = 1 mm, find R. Preserve the learner’s reasoning when revealing the explanation.

suggestions.title: Extension pathway
suggestions.proposal: Add an optional “Beyond this model” activity after the core task: Linear uncertainty propagation uses ∂R/∂r = r/h and ∂R/∂h = 1/2 − r²/(2h²). Near zero sag, reporting curvature can be more numerically useful than radius. State when it is a conceptual extension rather than something the current simulator calculates.

suggestions.title: Direct visual linkage
suggestions.proposal: Connect control focus to a highlight in time waveform linked to frequency spectrum; remove the highlight on blur so the visualization does not accumulate distracting emphasis.

suggestions.title: Predict before reveal
suggestions.proposal: In Predict, ask what happens to spectral peaks and fundamental frequency when one element of tone frequency and harmonic amplitudes changes; save the prediction and reveal the comparison only after the learner runs the case.

suggestions.title: Experiment checklist
suggestions.proposal: Turn this investigation into selectable steps with a recording slot per step: Compare sine, square and triangle spectra at equal RMS gain; inspect harmonics and leakage.

suggestions.title: Explain at the observation
suggestions.proposal: In Explain, place an expandable annotation beside time waveform linked to frequency spectrum that connects the visible behavior to: A periodic pressure signal can be decomposed into sinusoidal harmonics. Pitch relates primarily to repetition frequency; timbre depends on spectral composition. Sound-pressure level uses RMS pressure, not peak pressure.

suggestions.title: Challenge progression
suggestions.proposal: Offer a guided challenge about spectral peaks and fundamental frequency, then the same task with hints hidden; score the reasoning and final state separately.

suggestions.title: Tab continuity
suggestions.proposal: Preserve tone frequency and harmonic amplitudes, recorded evidence and scroll position when switching Observe, Predict, Experiment, Explain and Challenge; expose the active mode in a shareable URL.

suggestions.title: Tab interaction refinement
suggestions.proposal: For this lab’s mode strip, verify arrow-key navigation, visible focus, selected state and panel association; returning from theory should restore focus to the originating Sound Spectrum control.

suggestions.title: Equation-to-scene mapping
suggestions.proposal: Allow each term in “Lp=20 log10(prms/20 μPa); Δf=fs/N” to highlight its corresponding readout or element of time waveform linked to frequency spectrum; provide a plain-text explanation alongside symbols.

suggestions.title: Units drawer
suggestions.proposal: Add a compact units and symbols drawer next to the equation: Pressure in Pa; sample rate fs=48000 Hz; FFT size N=8192. Keep units visible even when that drawer is closed.

suggestions.title: Worked-example replay
suggestions.proposal: Make the existing worked example replayable as ordered steps, highlighting the substituted quantities before showing the result: For fs=48000 Hz and N=8192. Bin spacing=48000/8192. Δf=5.859375 Hz; doubling RMS pressure adds 6.0206 dB.

suggestions.title: Derivation stepper
suggestions.proposal: Present the derivation one step at a time with Back and Show all controls. The first annotated step should be: Represent the waveform as a harmonic sum.

suggestions.title: Misconception feedback
suggestions.proposal: When a prediction conflicts with the model, offer a targeted comparison around this misconception rather than a generic wrong-answer message: A larger FFT does not increase the sample rate; it increases observation duration and narrows bin spacing.

suggestions.title: Assumptions in context
suggestions.proposal: Place a concise model-limit badge beside spectral peaks and fundamental frequency; expand it to show: Periodic waveforms use a finite harmonic sum. Noise is a deterministic repeated digital buffer. The plotted acoustic pressure is simulated, not a microphone measurement.

suggestions.title: Paired comparison
suggestions.proposal: Let learners pin a baseline and compare a second setting of tone frequency and harmonic amplitudes; align the two views of time waveform linked to frequency spectrum and show changes in spectral peaks and fundamental frequency.

suggestions.title: Trial notebook
suggestions.proposal: Add a trial table that records tone frequency and harmonic amplitudes, spectral peaks and fundamental frequency and a learner note; include undo for removing a row and a clear indication of which trial is currently displayed.

suggestions.title: Inspectable evidence
suggestions.proposal: Provide an inspect mode for spectral peaks and fundamental frequency: synchronized cursor values for continuous plots, or selectable labeled rows for discrete states; keep the inspected point visible in time waveform linked to frequency spectrum.

suggestions.title: Reversible exploration
suggestions.proposal: Provide named baseline reset and one-step undo for changes to tone frequency and harmonic amplitudes; preview what a reset will replace when recorded trials are present.

suggestions.title: Narrow-screen layout
suggestions.proposal: On a narrow screen, keep time waveform linked to frequency spectrum above the primary tone frequency and harmonic amplitudes controls, and make spectral peaks and fundamental frequency available through a compact sticky summary without covering tab content.

suggestions.title: Redundant visual encoding
suggestions.proposal: Use labels plus line styles, shapes or arrowheads in time waveform linked to frequency spectrum; make the comparison understandable in grayscale and avoid relying on color alone.

suggestions.title: Accessible evidence summary
suggestions.proposal: Expose a readable summary of spectral peaks and fundamental frequency and the selected state of time waveform linked to frequency spectrum; announce user-triggered changes at a controlled rate rather than announcing every animation frame.

suggestions.title: Visual density control
suggestions.proposal: Offer essential and detailed annotation levels for time waveform linked to frequency spectrum; retain units and the main spectral peaks and fundamental frequency readout in both modes.

suggestions.title: Motion and rendering preference
suggestions.proposal: If time waveform linked to frequency spectrum animates, offer pause, slower playback and reduced-motion presentation; for a static view, offer a simplified rendering option that retains all numerical evidence.

suggestions.title: Reasoning self-check
suggestions.proposal: Present this self-check with an optional hint and a separate answer reveal: Which ideal square-wave harmonics are present? Preserve the learner’s reasoning when revealing the explanation.

suggestions.title: Extension pathway
suggestions.proposal: Add an optional “Beyond this model” activity after the core task: Zero padding interpolates the spectral plot but does not add physical resolving power. Window choice trades main-lobe width against sidelobe suppression. State when it is a conceptual extension rather than something the current simulator calculates.

suggestions.title: Reproducible sharing
suggestions.proposal: Create a share/export summary containing tone frequency and harmonic amplitudes, spectral peaks and fundamental frequency, model assumptions and lab version; offer a text alternative to the visual snapshot of time waveform linked to frequency spectrum.

suggestions.title: Studio learning connection
suggestions.proposal: End the session with a concise evidence-based recap of spectral peaks and fundamental frequency, the saved prediction and one next-lab link within Waves & Sound Studio; explain the conceptual connection before navigation.

suggestions.title: Direct visual linkage
suggestions.proposal: Connect control focus to a highlight in continuous field loops through the magnet; remove the highlight on blur so the visualization does not accumulate distracting emphasis.

suggestions.title: Predict before reveal
suggestions.proposal: In Predict, ask what happens to local field direction and relative strength when one element of magnet orientation and probe position changes; save the prediction and reveal the comparison only after the learner runs the case.

suggestions.title: Experiment checklist
suggestions.proposal: Turn this investigation into selectable steps with a recording slot per step: Reverse one magnet and inspect the field at the midpoint and off axis.

suggestions.title: Explain at the observation
suggestions.proposal: In Explain, place an expandable annotation beside continuous field loops through the magnet that connects the visible behavior to: A magnetic field has both magnitude and direction. A compass aligns with its local horizontal component. External bar-magnet fields can be approximated by dipoles away from the material, with return flux closing through the magnet.

suggestions.title: Challenge progression
suggestions.proposal: Offer a guided challenge about local field direction and relative strength, then the same task with hints hidden; score the reasoning and final state separately.

suggestions.title: Tab continuity
suggestions.proposal: Preserve magnet orientation and probe position, recorded evidence and scroll position when switching Observe, Predict, Experiment, Explain and Challenge; expose the active mode in a shareable URL.

suggestions.title: Tab interaction refinement
suggestions.proposal: For this lab’s mode strip, verify arrow-key navigation, visible focus, selected state and panel association; returning from theory should restore focus to the originating Field Lines control.

suggestions.title: Equation-to-scene mapping
suggestions.proposal: Allow each term in “B=(μ0/4πr³)[3(m·rhat)rhat−m]” to highlight its corresponding readout or element of continuous field loops through the magnet; provide a plain-text explanation alongside symbols.

suggestions.title: Units drawer
suggestions.proposal: Add a compact units and symbols drawer next to the equation: Dipole moment in A·m²; position in m; field in tesla. Keep units visible even when that drawer is closed.

suggestions.title: Worked-example replay
suggestions.proposal: Make the existing worked example replayable as ordered steps, highlighting the substituted quantities before showing the result: For m=1 A·m² on the axis at r=0.10 m. Baxis=2×10⁻⁷m/r³. Baxis=2×10⁻⁴ T=0.20 mT.

suggestions.title: Derivation stepper
suggestions.proposal: Present the derivation one step at a time with Back and Show all controls. The first annotated step should be: Resolve each dipole's moment along the observation direction.

suggestions.title: Misconception feedback
suggestions.proposal: When a prediction conflicts with the model, offer a targeted comparison around this misconception rather than a generic wrong-answer message: Outside a magnet, conventional field arrows run north to south, but magnetic field lines do not terminate at poles.

suggestions.title: Assumptions in context
suggestions.proposal: Place a concise model-limit badge beside local field direction and relative strength; expand it to show: Magnets are point-dipole approximations outside a masked core, not exact near-surface bar-magnet solutions. Direction is undefined at a field null.

suggestions.title: Paired comparison
suggestions.proposal: Let learners pin a baseline and compare a second setting of magnet orientation and probe position; align the two views of continuous field loops through the magnet and show changes in local field direction and relative strength.

suggestions.title: Trial notebook
suggestions.proposal: Add a trial table that records magnet orientation and probe position, local field direction and relative strength and a learner note; include undo for removing a row and a clear indication of which trial is currently displayed.

suggestions.title: Inspectable evidence
suggestions.proposal: Provide an inspect mode for local field direction and relative strength: synchronized cursor values for continuous plots, or selectable labeled rows for discrete states; keep the inspected point visible in continuous field loops through the magnet.

suggestions.title: Reversible exploration
suggestions.proposal: Provide named baseline reset and one-step undo for changes to magnet orientation and probe position; preview what a reset will replace when recorded trials are present.

suggestions.title: Narrow-screen layout
suggestions.proposal: On a narrow screen, keep continuous field loops through the magnet above the primary magnet orientation and probe position controls, and make local field direction and relative strength available through a compact sticky summary without covering tab content.

suggestions.title: Redundant visual encoding
suggestions.proposal: Use labels plus line styles, shapes or arrowheads in continuous field loops through the magnet; make the comparison understandable in grayscale and avoid relying on color alone.

suggestions.title: Accessible evidence summary
suggestions.proposal: Expose a readable summary of local field direction and relative strength and the selected state of continuous field loops through the magnet; announce user-triggered changes at a controlled rate rather than announcing every animation frame.

suggestions.title: Visual density control
suggestions.proposal: Offer essential and detailed annotation levels for continuous field loops through the magnet; retain units and the main local field direction and relative strength readout in both modes.

suggestions.title: Motion and rendering preference
suggestions.proposal: If continuous field loops through the magnet animates, offer pause, slower playback and reduced-motion presentation; for a static view, offer a simplified rendering option that retains all numerical evidence.

suggestions.title: Reasoning self-check
suggestions.proposal: Present this self-check with an optional hint and a separate answer reveal: Can magnetic fields cancel at a point? Preserve the learner’s reasoning when revealing the explanation.

suggestions.title: Extension pathway
suggestions.proposal: Add an optional “Beyond this model” activity after the core task: Gauss's law for magnetism is ∇·B=0. Drawing only exterior segments should not be mistaken for physical lines that begin and end on isolated magnetic charges. State when it is a conceptual extension rather than something the current simulator calculates.

suggestions.title: Reproducible sharing
suggestions.proposal: Create a share/export summary containing magnet orientation and probe position, local field direction and relative strength, model assumptions and lab version; offer a text alternative to the visual snapshot of continuous field loops through the magnet.

suggestions.title: Studio learning connection
suggestions.proposal: End the session with a concise evidence-based recap of local field direction and relative strength, the saved prediction and one next-lab link within Magnetism Studio; explain the conceptual connection before navigation.
